description: Eval test cases for the clean-pro-review-gates combined meta-skill

evals.name: gate-1-code-quality-swallowed-errors
evals.description: Gate 1 should flag broad catch-all error handling that swallows exceptions
evals.expected_output: Rule 15 violation: broad catch-all that swallows all exceptions. Catch only the specific error type you can recover from.
assertions: Detects broad except clause (except Exception, except Throwable, catch all)
Flags silent return of None/null as error swallowing
Suggests catching only the specific error type
Mentions Karpathy or 'swallowed errors' in reasoning

evals.name: gate-1-code-quality-hallucinated-import
evals.description: Gate 1 should flag imports that may not exist in the installed version
evals.test_input:
from langchain_community.vectorstores import Qdrant
from huggingface_cli import upload
evals.expected_output: Rule 17 / Rule 6 violation: verify every import against the installed version. AI-suggested package names may not exist or may be slopsquatting vectors.
assertions: Flags unknown or AI-suggested package imports
Suggests verifying against lockfile or installed packages
Mentions package hallucination research (USENIX Security '25)

evals.name: gate-1-code-quality-mock-fallback
evals.description: Gate 1 should flag hardcoded success returns in production code
evals.test_input:
def get_user_balance(user_id):
    return 1000  # TODO: actual provider call
evals.expected_output: Rule 18 violation: hardcoded 'success' return or fixture data in production code. Never return mock data from a function whose spec says it should perform real work.
assertions: Flags hardcoded return value as mock fallback
Flags TODO as cover for incomplete implementation
Suggests raising NotImplementedError or explicit unimplemented mechanism

evals.name: gate-1-code-quality-paint-by-numbers-comments
evals.description: Gate 1 should flag comments that restate the code instead of explaining why
evals.test_input:
# Increment counter by one
counter += 1

# Step 3: return the result
return result
evals.expected_output: Rule 5 violation: comments explain *why*, never *what*. Delete comments paraphrasing the line below them. Remove step-number scaffolding comments.
assertions: Flags 'what-comments' that restate obvious code
Flags step-number scaffolding comments
Suggests deleting or converting to 'why' commentary

evals.name: gate-1-code-quality-naming-violation
evals.description: Gate 1 should flag generic, intent-less names
evals.expected_output: Rule 1 violation: names must reveal intent. 'data', 'process_data', 'result', 'item', 'temp' are generic. Use domain-revealing names like 'double_prices(orders)'.
assertions: Flags 'data', 'result', 'item', 'temp' as generic names
Flags 'process_data' as verb without revealed intent
Suggests domain-specific replacement names

evals.name: gate-2-test-mock-of-internal-helper
evals.description: Gate 2 should flag mocks of internal helpers instead of system boundaries
evals.test_input:
def test_calculate_total():
    with patch('app.services.calculator._apply_tax') as mock_tax:
        mock_tax.return_value = 10.0
        result = calculator.calculate_total(100)
        mock_tax.assert_called_once_with(100)
evals.expected_output: Rule 1/Rule 2 violation: testing implementation details by mocking an internal helper. Assert the return value or observable side effect from the caller's perspective instead.
assertions: Flags mock of internal/private function as implementation test
Suggests asserting return value instead of mock call count
Notes that internal helper _apply_tax is not a system boundary

evals.name: gate-2-test-data-driven-opportunity
evals.description: Gate 2 should flag near-duplicate tests that should be merged into data-driven
evals.expected_output: Rule 3 violation: three tests share identical setup and differ only in input/output values. Merge into a single data-driven test using parametrize/data provider.
assertions: Detects near-identical test bodies
Suggests data-driven/parameterized test pattern
Notes shared setup and assertion pattern as merge signal

evals.name: gate-2-test-unjustified-constructor-test
evals.description: Gate 2 should flag tests that verify trivially obvious behavior
evals.test_input:
def test_user_constructor():
    user = User(name="Alice", email="alice@example.com")
    assert user.name == "Alice"
    assert user.email == "alice@example.com"
evals.expected_output: Rule 4 violation: this test catches no bug that wouldn't be caught by the type system or a single integration test. Test behavior, not attribute assignment.
assertions: Flags constructor/attribute tests as unjustified
Notes that the type system or a single integration test covers this
Suggests deleting the test or replacing with a behavior test

evals.name: gate-3-docs-symbol-verification
evals.description: Gate 3 should flag docs that reference symbols not in the source code
evals.test_input: The `POST /api/v2/invoices` endpoint returns a list of invoices. Use the `generate_report_v2()` helper to create PDFs.
evals.expected_output: Rule 1 violation: verify every referenced symbol against the actual source. If `POST /api/v2/invoices` or `generate_report_v2()` do not exist in the code, the docs contain false claims.
assertions: Flags unverifiable endpoint references
Flags unverifiable function references
Requires verification against actual source, not memory

evals.name: gate-3-docs-code-sample-runnable
evals.description: Gate 3 should flag code samples with imports that don't exist or hardcoded paths
evals.test_input:
```python
from nonexistent_library import process
result = process('/Users/alice/local/data.csv')
print(result)
```
evals.expected_output: Rule 2 violation: code sample must work on a clean machine. Import 'nonexistent_library' must be checked. Hardcoded local paths ('/Users/alice/...') must not ship.
assertions: Flags unverifiable imports in code samples
Flags hardcoded local paths
Requires sample to be runnable outside author's machine

evals.name: gate-4-security-sql-injection
evals.description: Gate 4 should flag SQL injection via string concatenation
evals.test_input:
query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '" + email + "'"
db.execute(query)
evals.expected_output: Rule 2 violation: string-built query with input is SQL injection. Use parameterized queries/prepared statements.
assertions: Flags string concatenation in SQL query
Suggests parameterized query
Maps to CWE-89

evals.name: gate-4-security-hardcoded-secret
evals.description: Gate 4 should flag hardcoded secrets in source code
evals.expected_output: Rule 11 violation: secret as literal in source code. Read from environment or secrets manager. Any secret that touched a commit is compromised — flag for rotation.
assertions: Flags hardcoded API keys and tokens
Suggests environment variable or secrets manager
Maps to CWE-798

evals.name: gate-4-security-missing-authorization
evals.description: Gate 4 should flag endpoints without server-side authorization checks
evals.test_input:
@app.get('/api/invoices/{id}')
async def get_invoice(id: int):
    invoice = await db.get(id)
    return invoice
evals.expected_output: Rule 7 violation: missing authorization check. Any logged-in user can access any invoice (IDOR). Verify the current principal owns or may act on the resource.
assertions: Flags missing ownership/permission check
Identifies IDOR vulnerability potential
Maps to CWE-862, CWE-639

evals.name: gate-5-infra-script-injection
evals.description: Gate 5 should flag untrusted context in shell inline
evals.test_input:
jobs:
  comment:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: "echo \"Issue: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}\""
evals.expected_output: Rule 1 violation: attacker-controlled workflow context interpolated directly into shell. Issue title is attacker-controllable; pass through env var and quote.
assertions: Flags ${{ }} interpolation in run: step
Identifies attacker-controlled context
Suggests env var passthrough as mitigation
Maps to CICD-SEC-4

evals.name: gate-5-infra-unpinned-action
evals.description: Gate 5 should flag third-party actions pinned to a moving tag
evals.test_input:
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - uses: docker/login-action@v2
  - uses: actions/setup-node@main
evals.expected_output: Rule 4 violation: third-party actions pinned to a moving tag or branch (@v4, @v2, @main). Pin to a full commit SHA to prevent supply-chain hijack.
assertions: Flags moving tag pinning
Flags branch pinning ('@main')
Suggests SHA pinning with version comment
Maps to CICD-SEC-3
